omitted.reason: The OpenClaw inbound pipeline: allowlist name resolution against the friend/group directory, route resolution, pairing/DM/group policy, the group history window, the delivered/seen acks, the typing indicator, the `ctxPayload` build, `core.channel.inbound.dispatch` and the reply-delivery closure, plus the provider lifecycle around them. The Hub owns every one of those. Replaced at the smallest boundary by `fusion/inbound-adapter.ts`, `fusion/admission.ts`, `fusion/listener-session.ts` and `lifecycle/start-account.ts` (D-ZU-013/014/015/020); the listener itself (`startZaloListener`) is carried verbatim inside `zalo-js.ts`. Consequence: the typing indicator and the delivered/seen acks are wired on the client (`send.ts`) but not driven, and the inbound-media download is not carried (Zalo Personal inbound attachments arrive as message content, not as a URL the vertical fetches).

The durable ingress monitor: it opens OpenClaw's SQLite-backed `openChannelIngressQueue`, appends the serialized `zca-js` envelope and runs its own drain with retry policy, dead-letter and claim lifecycle. The Hub already owns that store and that drain — `channel_ingress_queue` with lease/fencing, per-lane ordering, retry, dead-letter and restart drain (goal slices 1 and 8) — so the module is replaced by `fusion/admission.ts` (D-ZU-014), which keeps everything upstream DECIDES: the envelope inspection (`data.msgId` as the event id, `group:<idTo>` / `direct:<uidFrom>` as the lane key), the payload-error taxonomy and the authentication-failure classification.
An in-memory `ChannelIngressQueue` double for the omitted `ingress.ts`. The Fusion admission is tested against a fake inbound processor instead (`fusion/admission.test.ts`).

The OpenClaw `ChannelPlugin` definition: capabilities, config adapter, directory, status adapter, pairing, threading and the outbound delivery profile. Fusion's drive surface is `plugin.ts` and the Hub owns config, status, pairing, policy and delivery. The parts that are behaviour and not host wiring are carried where they are read: the 2000-char chunk limit (`channel.adapters.ts` / `outbound.ts`), the target prefixes (`session-route.ts`), the capability list (HUB-WIRING.md §1).
The OpenClaw setup-wizard trampoline for `setup-surface.ts`. The Hub owns onboarding; the QR verbs it needs are `fusion/qr-setup.ts` (D-ZU-016).

`createZalouserPluginBase`: the OpenClaw plugin meta, capability list, config adapter, `configSchema` and `doctor` wiring. Every consumer is the omitted `channel.ts`; the Hub owns the catalog entry, the config schema and the status surface.

The zod channel-config schema OpenClaw validates `config.json` with. The Hub compiles and validates channel config (`packages/hub/src/channels/config/compile.ts`); the field list this vertical actually reads is documented in HUB-WIRING.md §4.
The OpenClaw `doctor` entry point for this channel. The Hub owns the health/status surface; the account probe it needs is `probe.ts`, carried verbatim.
The `doctor` contract descriptor (which config paths the wizard may fix). Hub-owned onboarding, same reason as `doctor.ts`.
OpenClaw `doctor`/status issue builders. The Hub owns the status surface.
The OpenClaw setup adapter/wizard proxy (config promotion, account patching, dm-policy writes). The Hub owns onboarding.

The interactive OpenClaw setup wizard surface: it drives the QR login by printing a temp-file path and blocking for three minutes. The Hub owns onboarding, and the same state machine is exposed as non-blocking verbs by `fusion/qr-setup.ts` (D-ZU-016).
Test doubles for the omitted setup surface.

The OpenClaw `doctor` config-audit findings for mutable group-name entries in `channels.zalouser.groups`. The Hub owns the config-audit surface, and the ID-vs-name matching rule the audit warns about is carried where it is enforced (`group-policy.ts`, `channel.adapters.ts`).
`resolveZalouserDmSessionScope`: maps OpenClaw's `session.dmScope` config onto a DM session scope. The Hub owns session scoping and session keys, the same cut `session-route.ts` makes (D-ZU-007).

The OpenClaw global plugin runtime store (`createPluginRuntimeStore`), which backs SQLite keyed stores from the OpenClaw state directory. Its two jobs in Fusion are split across `runtime-store.ts` (the injected `HostRuntime` and the per-account inbound processor, D-ZU-002) and `fusion/session-store.ts` (the credential store, D-ZU-004), so no ported file calls `getZalouserRuntime()` and keeping an inactive copy would be dead code.

deviations.reason: `runtime-api.ts` — upstream's file is the plugin's OpenClaw host binding: ~40 re-exports of `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` (the setup wizard, the pairing controller, the reply pipeline, the config contracts, the plugin runtime setter) so a bundled plugin can be loaded without importing `openclaw`. Fusion has no OpenClaw host; the members this vertical's closure reads come from `@getpaseo/channels-core`, which mirrors the same upstream source modules. Kept at the same name and job so the ported files keep upstream's import block; the Hub-owned members (setup, pairing, reply delivery, doctor) are dropped rather than re-implemented.

Upstream holds the plugin runtime in one process-global slot (`runtime.ts`), because it runs one Zalo Personal account per OpenClaw process. The Hub runs every account of every organization in one process, each with its own `HostRuntime`, keyed stores and logger, so the runtime and the per-account L3 inbound processor are keyed by account id. Same shape as the Google Chat, Discord, Telegram and Zalo verticals' `runtime-store.ts`.

tsconfig: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and `noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature` are off so the upstream Zalo Personal source compiles verbatim; OpenClaw's own tsconfig sets neither flag. Same cut the Discord (D-DC-001), Google Chat (D-GC-001) and Zalo (D-ZL-009) verticals make.

Session/credential persistence. A Zalo Personal account has no token: the QR login returns an `imei`, a cookie jar and a user agent, and those bytes ARE the account. Upstream keeps them in OpenClaw's SQLite-backed plugin state (`openSyncKeyedStore`, namespace `credentials`) reached through the global plugin runtime store. Fusion injects a `ZalouserSessionStore` instead; the shipped implementation is `createHostRuntimeSessionStore` over the account's `HostRuntime.state.openKeyedStore`, and the Hub owns encryption at rest behind it (runtime strategy §0.1 note 7 — QR-login session files keep native storage semantics with encrypted-at-rest storage, they are NOT forced into the Hub DB; HUB-WIRING.md §6). The port keeps upstream's SYNCHRONOUS `lookup`/`register`/`update` surface over a cache hydrated at account start, with write-behind to the store, so the ~1900-line `zalo-js.ts` credential closure is unchanged. `flushZalouserSessions()` awaits the pending writes and rethrows the first failure; the QR-login and logout verbs flush before they report success, so an operator is never told the account is linked while the credentials are still in flight. A background refresh that cannot be persisted stays best-effort, which is upstream's own rule.

`resolveLegacyZalouserCredentialsDir` / `resolveLegacyZalouserCredentialsPath` are dropped. They resolve OpenClaw's own state directory so `doctor` can detect (and refuse to resurrect) a pre-plugin-state credentials file. Fusion has no OpenClaw state dir and no such file to migrate; the durable revocation marker that makes the refusal work IS carried. The ported test case that asserted the legacy blob is absent asserts the injected store instead.

`resolvePreferredOpenClawTmpDir` — upstream walks its own tmp-root preference order (configured OpenClaw tmp root, then the state dir, then the OS temp dir). The single caller (`qr-temp-file.ts`) needs one thing: a private directory to drop the QR PNG in for an operator on the host. The boundary keeps the call shape and the private-directory guarantee over `os.tmpdir()`, with `ZALOUSER_TMP_DIR` as the override. The stable per-profile file name, the base64 decode, the 0600 mode and the overwrite-instead-of-accumulate rule are unchanged.

`resolveZalouserOutboundSessionRoute` is dropped: it maps a `zalouser:` target onto an OpenClaw AGENT SESSION KEY through `buildChannelOutboundSessionRoute`, and the Hub owns routing and session keys (the same cut the Zalo Official Bot vertical makes by omitting its whole `session-route.ts`). The three target parsers — `normalizeZalouserTarget`, `parseZalouserOutboundTarget`, `parseZalouserDirectoryGroupId` — stay verbatim, because the tool, the message actions, the outbound bridge and the directory all read them. Upstream's test file only exercised the dropped function, so it is replaced by a Fusion test over the parsers.

`withTimeout` — upstream reads it from `plugin-sdk/security-runtime`, which re-exports it from the `@openclaw/fs-safe` workspace package. Fusion never depends on an OpenClaw workspace package, and `@getpaseo/channels-core`'s `security-runtime` boundary deliberately stops at the secret-compare and external-content members (D-CORE-244). The two ported call sites (restoring a session, and the session health check) need one behaviour — reject with a named message when the promise outruns its budget — so the boundary keeps that call shape. NOT carried: cancelling the underlying work, which upstream does not do here either (`zca-js` exposes no abort for a login).

Upstream's file is the whole OpenClaw `ChannelPlugin` adapter set. The carried half is what is still channel behaviour: `sendZalouserTextFromContext` / `sendZalouserMediaFromContext` (the send path Fusion's `outbound.ts` drives, with upstream's markdown text mode and chunk limits), `zalouserMessageActions` (the `react` action), `zalouserResolverAdapter` (friend/group name → id), `zalouserAuthAdapter` (the QR login driver), `zalouserGroupsAdapter` and `zalouserMessagingAdapter`. DROPPED with their OpenClaw owners: `zalouserMessageAdapter` (`defineChannelMessageAdapter`), `zalouserRawSendResultAdapter` / `zalouserOutboundAdapter` (the reply pipeline's payload sender), `resolveZalouserDmPolicy` / `zalouserSecurityAdapter` (DM policy + config audit), `zalouserPairingTextAdapter` (pairing) and `zalouserThreadingAdapter` (Zalo Personal has no thread primitive; upstream pins `replyToMode: "off"` and `outbound.ts` states the same rule). `zalouserMessagingAdapter.resolveOutboundSessionRoute` goes with D-ZU-007, and its `isNumericTargetId` call becomes the decimal test that helper performs.

`resolveZalouserOutboundChunkMode` / `resolveZalouserOutboundTextChunkLimit` — upstream reads them from `getZalouserRuntime().channel.text.*`, an OpenClaw host function over the process config. Fusion reads the same two knobs (`textChunkMode`, `textChunkLimit`) off the account's compiled config entry and falls back to upstream's defaults (`length` mode, 2000 characters).

`collectZalouserSecurityAuditFindings` is dropped from the lazy runtime module with `security-audit.ts` (the OpenClaw `doctor` config-audit surface the Hub owns). Every other member is carried, so the module keeps upstream's name and job.

Account resolution input. Upstream reads OpenClaw's process-wide `config.json` (`channels.zalouser.accounts.<id>` plus `ZALOUSER_PROFILE` / `ZCA_PROFILE`); in Fusion the Hub supervisor compiles the account's config revision and hands the vertical the flat `ctx.account` carrier plus the `cfg.channels.zalouser.accounts.<id>` entry. This module is the ONLY reader of those carrier field names (`profile` / `zcaProfile`, `name`), so the Hub wiring slice has one file to match (HUB-WIRING.md §5). Unlike every other channel, the carrier holds NO secret: the credential is the QR session behind the profile, and it lives in the session store (D-ZU-004). The ported `accounts.ts` keeps its upstream shape and flow.

`monitor.ts`'s inbound normalization. Upstream resolves the route, runs the pairing/allowlist/group policy, builds the history window, assembles the OpenClaw `ctxPayload` and calls `core.channel.inbound.dispatch`. The Hub owns all of that, so this module only turns the already-normalized `ZaloInboundMessage` (upstream's own `normalizeZaloInboundMessage`, carried verbatim in `zalo-js.ts`) into the shared `ChannelInboundEvent` (kind + facts). Carried from upstream: the group/direct split, the timestamp rule, the mention extraction and the mention-stripped command body — all of them inside `normalizeZaloInboundMessage`. DECIDED here, because the Hub reads them: (1) the external message id is the `msgId:cliMsgId` PAIR, because `addReaction` needs both and collapsing to `msgId` would make an inbound message un-reactable; (2) `wasMentioned` folds upstream's explicit mention, its implicit (quote-of-own-message) mention and its "cannot attribute the mention" fallback into the single fact the Hub's mention policy reads; (3) a leading `/verb` in the mention-stripped body is `kind: "command"`, since Zalo Personal has no native command surface.

Durable admission. Replaces upstream's `ingress.ts` (OpenClaw's SQLite ingress queue plus its own drain) with the Hub queue via the shared inbound processor, and keeps the receive contract the listener session depends on: `durable`, `ignored` (a well-formed non-turn message), `invalid` (never retried), THROW (admission did not happen). Everything that decides WHAT an envelope is stays verbatim: `inspectZalouserIngressMessage` (the `data.msgId` event id, the `group:<idTo>` / `direct:<uidFrom>` lane key, the unsupported-thread-type refusal), the payload-error class and `isZalouserAuthenticationFailure`.

L2 transport session. Upstream's `startZaloListener` is carried verbatim inside `zalo-js.ts` (the self-message filter, the message/error/closed handlers, the 30s watchdog with its 35s max gap, `retryOnClose: false`, the API invalidation on failure and the abort-driven cleanup); this module owns the part upstream delegated to its own durable queue. THE ONE ADDED RULE: the `zca-js` listener is a push socket with no ack and no cursor, so admission must complete before the message handler returns, and a failed admission is retried in place up to `ZALOUSER_ADMISSION_MAX_ATTEMPTS` before the message is dropped with an error-level line — the provider cannot re-serve it. That is the honest limit of a QR/session channel, and it is why the drop is loud.

The QR setup surface. Upstream's driver is `zalouserAuthAdapter.login`: start the QR, write the PNG to a temp file, print the path, then BLOCK in `waitForZaloQrLogin` for up to three minutes — a CLI's shape. The state machine itself is upstream's and is not re-implemented (`startZaloQrLogin` / `waitForZaloQrLogin` / `logoutZaloProfile` in `zalo-js.ts`, unchanged, including the QR TTL, the expiry retry, the pending-login re-attach and the owner check that stops one setup turn adopting another's login). This module exposes it as five non-blocking verbs the Hub can call from an RPC — start, poll, cancel, relink (upstream's `force`), logout — maps upstream's states onto `pending` / `linked` / `failed`, and FLUSHES the session store before reporting `linked`.

Tool registration. Upstream registers the `zalouser` agent tool through the OpenClaw plugin host (`extensions/zalouser/index.ts` `registerFull(api)`); reading only the channel plugin object would miss that path (2026-09-06 channel-tools audit §6). Fusion has no plugin host, so this module exposes the same two surfaces the Feishu vertical does over the same registrar shape: `zalouserAgentTools` (the factory list) and `registerZalouserTools(registrar)`. The tool itself — name, schema, description, executor, result shapes — is the ported `tool.ts`, untouched. It stays a per-execution FACTORY because `createZalouserTool(context)` binds the delivery context that decides which conversation an ambient send lands in.

The Hub's `plugin.outbound.*` bridge onto the carried `channel.adapters.ts` send helpers. Every wire decision — the markdown text mode and its style ranges, the 2000-char chunking with per-chunk style slicing, the media/voice branch and the receipt shape — lives in the ported source. `sendMedia` posts NATIVELY (unlike the Zalo Official Bot vertical, the personal-account client has `uploadAttachment`), and pins `mediaLocalRoots` to the file's own directory so the ported loader cannot be asked for a path outside it. Zalo Personal has no thread primitive, so `threadId` is ignored.

The `message` tool surface. Upstream's `zalouserMessageActions` adapter is carried unchanged in `channel.adapters.ts` and advertises exactly one action, `react`, which is the only message mutation the personal-account client exposes beyond a plain send (`api.addReaction`). This module adds only the drive-time account carrier fold, so `fusion/account-config.ts` stays the single reader of the Hub's carrier field names, and pins the supported-action set so the Hub answers `unsupported_action` for everything else.

L4 lifecycle. Upstream's `monitorZalouserProvider` prologue is carried: the own-user-id resolution before any message is normalized, the ready status patch, and the listener-failure-fails-the-account rule. The OpenClaw pieces — the SQLite ingress queue, the allowlist/group name resolution against the friend and group directories, the pairing controller, the reply pipeline and the history window — are Hub-owned. ONE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: an unlinked profile FAILS the start (upstream comes up and reports `not authenticated` through `doctor`), because the Hub supervisor has no other place to learn the QR session is gone and a silently-idle account is the failure mode an operator would not see. The session store is installed and hydrated before anything reads a credential, and uninstalled when the account stops.

`OpenClawPluginToolContext` — `@getpaseo/channels-core` carries the tool context as a host adapter that narrows away upstream's two runtime-config readers (`runtimeConfig`, `getRuntimeConfig`). The ported `tool.ts` prefers them over `config` so a media ceiling changed mid-session is honoured, so the barrel restores upstream's spelling by intersection rather than editing the ported file.

`resolveChannelMediaMaxBytes` — upstream's barrel `plugin-sdk/account-helpers` re-exports it, and `@getpaseo/channels-core` deliberately omits that member (D-CORE-303, "the Hub owns media ceilings"). The ported `accounts.ts` and `tool.ts` still need the ACCOUNT-level ceiling, which is channel config and not a Hub policy, so upstream's `src/channels/plugins/media-limits.ts` is carried here with its body and call shape. The one line that changes is `normalizeAccountId`, which upstream imports from its session-key module; the boundary inlines the trim-or-`default` it performs.

One ported test expectation moves with the core probe boundary: `@getpaseo/channels-core` carries `runChannelProbe` with its own rejection text (`timed out after Nms`) where upstream's is a bare `timeout`. The invariant the case exists for — the probe fails instead of hanging, and reports an elapsed time — is asserted unchanged.

One ported test expectation moves with the core outbound-media boundary: `@getpaseo/channels-core`'s `loadOutboundMediaFromUrl` refuses an oversized file with `… is N bytes, over the M byte limit` where upstream's message is `exceeds limit`. The invariant the case exists for — the account media cap is applied BEFORE the native send, so nothing is posted — is asserted unchanged.
